text: Why must a deep neural network include nonlinear activation functions between its linear layers?
choices: Because linear layers cannot be implemented in optics
Because otherwise the weights would all become negative
Because a cascade of linear maps collapses to a single matrix W_eff, giving the network the expressivity of only one layer
Because nonlinearities reduce the number of MACs required
explanation: If f were the identity, W^(L)...W^(1) equals a single W_eff, so depth adds nothing; the nonlinearity is the entire source of a deep network's power. Linear layers are exactly what optics does well (option 0 is backwards), and nonlinearity has nothing to do with weight sign or MAC count.
